message.content:
**Answer:**  
The sculpture most frequently cited as the icon of the 19th‑century art world is **“The Thinker” by Auguste Rodin**. Created in the late 1800s (the original bronze cast dates from 1902–03, but the design was conceived in 1880), it has become the quintessential symbol of modern sculpture and is recognized worldwide.  

*(Other contenders include Rodin’s “The Kiss” (1889) and the monumental “Gates of Hell” series, but “The Thinker” remains the most universally celebrated.)*
